"Triple Red 7s Multiplier" has had no $77,777 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "Triple Red 7s Multiplier" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
802.headline: No new top prize claims

803.body:
The prize money on "Triple Red 777s" leans toward the smaller prizes. It is spread over thirteen prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Tomorrow's count on "Triple Red 777s" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
803.headline: How the prize money is divided

804.body:
"Diamond Bingo" has five of seven top prizes left and is in the middle of its run. About a third of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Everything here about "Diamond Bingo" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 23.
804.headline: Where this game is in its run

805.body:
"Multiply Your Money" has gone over a month without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $50,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Today's free summary of "Multiply Your Money" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
805.headline: Good news: no big claims

806.body:
"Win $50, $100 or $200" is near the midpoint of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Today's free summary of "Win $50, $100 or $200" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
806.headline: Where this game is in its run

807.body:
A $20,000 top prize on "Ravens X2" was claimed last week. The game started with four top prizes and has two top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "Ravens X2" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
807.headline: The top prize list got shorter

808.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Ravens X10", about half are still unsold. The game is about halfway through its run, with three of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything above about "Ravens X10" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
808.headline: Tickets sold so far

809.body:
One of Gold Bar Bingo's top prizes was claimed yesterday. A player in Maryland won $50,000. The game started with seven top prizes and now has five top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

If "Gold Bar Bingo" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
809.headline: Another top prize was claimed

810.body:
"In the Green" is down to five top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed last week. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

The numbers for "In the Green" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

812.headline: A top prize was just claimed

813.body:
The most common win left on "The Price is Right™" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $5,000, and eight of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything here about "The Price is Right™" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 23.

814.headline: The top prize list got shorter

815.body:
"$100,000 Crossword" has eight of nine top prizes left and is early in its run. About a quarter of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

The table below shows the full count for "$100,000 Crossword", with every prize level included.

If you play "Deluxe Crossword" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

"Season's Greetings" has joined the Maryland lineup at $2 with six top prizes of $10,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

821.headline: New in stores

822.body:
"Peppermint Payout" just went on sale in Maryland. The game has nine full prize levels with six top prizes of $30,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

The numbers for "Peppermint Payout" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
822.headline: New game, all prizes left

823.body:
"Holly-Day Cash" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $5 game with seven top prizes of $50,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

Everything here about "Holly-Day Cash" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 23.
823.headline: Brand new, no claims yet

824.body:
"Winter Multiplier" just reached Maryland stores with nine top prizes of $100,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

Tomorrow's count on "Winter Multiplier" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
